title: NVIDIA publishes a practical path to GPU-scale robot simulation
friendlyTitle: NVIDIA explains how to run many robot simulations on a GPU
summary: NVIDIA’s tutorial shows how Warp and MJWarp can move MuJoCo-based robotics simulations from CPU execution to batched GPU workloads. It explains the stack, code structure and decision points for teams preparing many parallel simulated environments before training a policy.
friendlySummary: The tutorial shows developers how to move familiar robot simulations onto NVIDIA GPUs and run many copies at once. It covers setup and preparation before training the robot’s control system.
whyItMatters: Robot-learning teams often need to run many simulated worlds, not merely one world faster. The guide gives developers a concrete way to scale familiar MuJoCo assets while retaining Python-based workflows and interoperability with training frameworks.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Running more simulations can help teams test robot behaviour faster and reduce expensive trial-and-error with physical machines.
